title: Halloween, framing
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: Halloween. The town one block wide still, then not. A kid in a sheet on main street, the same kid or another. 'What are you?' Last year: auditing. This year, in the chore coat: 'Framing.' The kid says that's not a costume. Wood says give it time.

panels.composition: Main street, Halloween, rain in vertical hatching, pumpkins under the hardware store's awning. WOOD in the chore coat, hands in the pockets. BARNABY. A KID in a sheet.

image.prompt: a rainy small-town main street on Halloween with pumpkins under a store awning, a young man in an oversized canvas chore coat with his hands in the pockets, a small dog, a child in a bedsheet, black and white, no words
a small child in a bedsheet ghost costume looking up at a young man, black and white, no words
a child in a sheet, unimpressed, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The kid going on with the pillowcase. Wood and the dog. The street: four blocks again, the strip checked. The coat. Give it time.

image.prompt: a child in a sheet walking away down a rainy street as a young man in a chore coat and a small dog stand under an awning, black and white, no words
